stem: A tank containing 500 liters of water is drained through a valve at its base. The volume \(V\), in liters, of water remaining in the tank \(t\) minutes after the valve is opened is modeled by \(V = 500\left(1 - \frac{t}{20}\right)^{2}\) for \(0 \le t \le 20\). According to the model, how many minutes after the valve is opened does the tank contain 250 liters of water?
solution: For \(0 \le t \le 20\), \(1 - \frac{t}{20} \ge 0\), so take the positive root: \(1 - \frac{t}{20} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\).
Then \(\frac{t}{20} = 1 - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), so \(t = 20 - 10\sqrt{2} \approx 5.9\) minutes. The tank drains faster at first, so it is half empty well before the halfway time.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of assuming the tank drains at a constant rate, so that half the water is gone at half of 20 minutes; the model is quadratic, and \(V(10) = 125\), not \(250\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of solving \(\frac{t}{20} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), dropping the \(1 -\) in \(1 - \frac{t}{20}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of taking the negative root \(1 - \frac{t}{20} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\); it is greater than 20, outside the interval on which the model applies.

verify:
t = symbols('t', real=True)
sols = [s for s in solve(Eq(500*(1 - t/20)**2, 250), t) if 0 <= s <= 20]
assert len(sols) == 1 and simplify(sols[0] - (20 - 10*sqrt(2))) == 0
assert simplify(value(choices[answer]) - sols[0]) == 0
assert all(simplify(value(choices[k]) - sols[0]) != 0 for k in choices if k != answer)
assert 500*(1 - Rational(10, 20))**2 == 125
